steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Meta-learning
- learning-to-learn / meta-learning: increasing interest in ML community in recent years
- vs conventional learning from scratch with static algorithm: leverage past experience on related tasks to improve future learning
- exploit shared structure between problems; hard deep learning problems where data and compute are limited/expensive

2. What has been meta-learned
- many approaches for components of deep neural networks
- early: optimization learning rules
- more recent: activation functions, fast adaptation parameter initializations, neural network architectures, whole learning algorithms from scratch, many more

3. Loss function
- overlooked until very recently
- networks trained mainly by backpropagation of gradients from loss function -> essential role
- typical: pick heuristically from modest set of hand-crafted losses -> should be reconsidered; principled, data-informed, task-specific

4. EvoMAL
- Evolved Model-Agnostic Loss (EvoMAL): meta-learns symbolic loss functions, hybrid neuro-symbolic search
- unifies two divergent lines of research: gradient-based vs evolution-based
- task and model-agnostic: any technique amenable to gradient descent style training; different architectures

Contributions
- (1) task/model-agnostic search space of primitive mathematical operations + genetic programming-based search for symbolic losses
- (2) first direct connection between expression tree-based symbolic losses and gradient trainable loss networks; parameterize + convert
- (3) unrolled differentiation as gradient-based local search; first computationally tractable approach to further optimizing symbolic losses

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
In recent years learning-to-learn, or meta-learning, has become an area that the machine learning community is more and more interested in. Conventional learning approaches learn from scratch with a static learning algorithm, but meta-learning gives a different paradigm where intelligent systems use their past experiences on related tasks to improve how they learn in the future. This paradigm has made it possible to use the shared structure between problems to tackle some deep learning problems that are traditionally very hard, in domains where data and computational resources are both limited and expensive to get.

Many meta-learning approaches have been proposed for optimizing different components of deep neural networks. For example, early research on this topic used meta-learning to generate optimization learning rules. More recent research has gone on to learn everything from activation functions, fast adaptation parameter initializations, and neural network architectures, to whole learning algorithms from scratch, and many more.

But one component that was overlooked until very recently is the loss function. In deep learning, neural networks are mostly trained by backpropagating gradients that come from the loss function, so loss functions play an essential role in training neural networks. Because they are so important, the usual approach of picking a loss function heuristically from a modest set of hand-crafted loss functions should be reconsidered, and instead there should be a more principled, data-informed approach that uses task-specific information to optimize the selection.

This paper tries to develop such an approach. We propose a new framework for learning loss functions called Evolved Model-Agnostic Loss (EvoMAL), which meta-learns symbolic loss functions with a hybrid neuro-symbolic search approach. This new approach unifies two lines of research on this topic that used to be divergent, and before this method they used only a gradient-based approach or only an evolution-based approach. Also, the framework is both task and model-agnostic, since it can be applied to any technique that is amenable to a gradient descent style training procedure and it works with different model architectures.

## Contributions

- (1) We design a task and model-agnostic search space made of primitive mathematical operations, and a genetic programming-based search algorithm for it, to learn symbolic loss functions.

- (2) We make the first direct connection between expression tree-based symbolic loss functions and gradient trainable loss networks, and so we propose a procedure for parameterizing the loss functions and converting them into trainable loss networks.

- (3) We use unrolled differentiation, a gradient-based local-search approach, to optimize the symbolic loss functions further. This is the first computationally tractable approach to further optimizing symbolic loss functions.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
The field of learning-to-learn, or meta-learning, has been an area of increasing interest to the machine learning community in recent years [1,2]. In contrast to conventional learning approaches, which learn from scratch using a static learning algorithm, meta-learning offers an alternative paradigm in which intelligent systems leverage their past experiences on related tasks to improve future learning performance [3]. This paradigm has made it possible to exploit the shared structure between problems to tackle several traditionally very challenging deep learning problems in domains where both data and computational resources are limited and expensive to procure [4,5].

Many meta-learning approaches have been proposed for optimizing various components of deep neural networks. For example, early research on the topic explored meta-learning for generating optimization learning rules [6,7,8,9]. More recent research has extended to learning everything from activation functions [10], fast adaptation parameter initializations [11,12,13], and neural network architectures [14,15,16,17] to whole learning algorithms from scratch [18,19], and many more (see [3]).

However, one component that has been overlooked until very recently is the loss function [20]. In deep learning, neural networks are predominantly trained through the backpropagation of gradients originating from the loss function [21]; hence, loss functions play an essential role in training neural networks. Given this importance, the typical approach of selecting a loss function heuristically from a modest set of hand-crafted loss functions should be reconsidered in favor of a more principled, data-informed approach that uses task-specific information to optimize the selection process.

This paper aims to develop such an approach: we propose a new framework for loss function learning called Evolved Model-Agnostic Loss (EvoMAL), which meta-learns symbolic loss functions via a hybrid neuro-symbolic search approach. This approach unifies two previously divergent lines of research on the topic, which, prior to this method, used either a gradient-based or an evolution-based approach exclusively. Furthermore, the proposed framework is both task and model-agnostic, as it can be applied to any technique amenable to a gradient descent style training procedure and is compatible with different model architectures.

## Contributions

- (1) A task and model-agnostic search space composed of primitive mathematical operations, together with a corresponding genetic programming-based search algorithm, is designed for learning symbolic loss functions.

- (2) We make the first direct connection between expression tree-based symbolic loss functions and gradient trainable loss networks, and accordingly propose a procedure for parameterizing and converting the loss functions into trainable loss networks.

- (3) Unrolled differentiation, a gradient-based local-search approach, is used to further optimize the symbolic loss functions. The proposed method is the first computationally tractable approach to further optimizing symbolic loss functions.
